A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TC-λ research. Their text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–B are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: V1 reports original Markov-chain simulations, text-classification experiments on four datasets, and GSM8K verifier and test-time-scaling experiments.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and reports additional squared-loss comparator results and GSM8K predictive negative log-likelihood results.

M1.justification: The TC-λ targets and objective, classifier architecture, Algorithm 1 training procedure and boosted best-of-N inference procedure are unchanged. The squared-loss variants are added comparison methods, not revisions to the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same layered Markov-chain simulation, OHSUMED, NEWSGROUPS, IMDB, AG-NEWS and GSM8K tasks. V2's description of AG-NEWS as three-way classification is a textual error: Table 2 retains four classes in both versions.

E2.justification: V2 adds direct ℓ2 loss and LSTD(λ) to the four-dataset comparison and GSM8K verifier evaluation (Table 1; Figures 5, 6 and 8). These introduce directly relevant Monte Carlo and temporal-difference regression comparators absent from v1's evaluated set. All earlier comparators remain.

E3.justification: The documented splits, model sizes, prefix lengths, generation procedure, optimization and model-selection settings remain unchanged. The added comparators use the corresponding existing hyperparameter configurations. GSM8K NLL results are newly displayed, but NLL was already part of Appendix B.1's evaluation framework; this does not establish a revised protocol.

E4.justification: V2 adds a focused comparison of cross-entropy with softmax against squared loss without softmax, examining both discrimination and predictive probability quality across prefixes. Figure 8 adds the GSM8K NLL analysis. Existing model-size, λ-sensitivity, temporal-inconsistency and illustrative-generation analyses remain.

E5.justification: V2 changes Figure 6's reporting description from standard errors to 95% confidence intervals and explicitly documents intervals and run counts in more captions. Figure 3 specifies five runs for the λ sweep; the checklist defines intervals as 1.96 times standard error. Table 1 drops significance-qualified highlighting. Appendix B.1 still states standard deviations and ten runs generally, leaving inconsistencies; an actual increase in runs is not established.

E6.justification: All original Table 1 values remain, but new comparator results substantially expand the evidence across the existing tasks. For OHSUMED four-token accuracy, direct ℓ2 and LSTD(λ) score 30.3 and 32.7, alongside unchanged DCE and TC-λ scores of 30.5 and 33.7. Figures 5–6 add squared-loss curves, and Figure 8 newly reports GSM8K NLL. V2 also quantifies training-time differences as within 1% and removes v1's informal observation of more stable training and less overfitting.

T1.justification: V2 makes the consistency assumption explicit: every transient state must have nonzero probability of being sampled under the initial-state and transition distributions. V1 referred only to mild assumptions. The propositions, mathematical development and Appendix A proofs otherwise remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and concluding discussion retain the same principal contributions: TC-λ training, theoretical data-efficiency benefits, improved incremental classification and more efficient LLM verification. The new comparisons support these claims without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: Section 3 adds a concrete explanation of how distinct text prefixes reaching similar semantic states could enable data pooling beyond tabular models. Sections 4 and B.3 add interpretations concerning class count, loss choice and predictive calibration. Existing limitations concerning model scale and application coverage remain substantively unchanged.

D1.justification: Tables 3 and 4 add batch sizes, epochs, learning rates, warmup, weight decay and λ settings for the squared-loss comparators. Existing implementation and hardware disclosures remain. The new checklist states an intention to release code, but does not establish that code is already available.

R1.justification: V2 adds Bertsekas and Tsitsiklis's Neuro-Dynamic Programming and Bradtke and Barto's least-squares temporal-difference work, connecting the theory to stochastic shortest paths and the comparisons to classical value estimation. The broader related-work narrative and novelty positioning remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 introduces a numbered Section 2.2, adds localized explanatory passages and a NeurIPS checklist, and updates contact/publication text. The main narrative, section sequence and most prose are retained rather than extensively rewritten.

P2.justification: Tables 1, 3 and 4 gain comparator rows; Figures 5 and 6 gain squared-loss curves and revised legends; Figure 8 is new. Several captions clarify uncertainty, and figures, tables and appendix material are repositioned. The overall visual format remains substantially the same.

improvement.justification: V1 motivated cross-entropy over squared-loss TD approaches without directly evaluating their counterparts. V2 adds these relevant comparisons and probability-quality results, strengthening the empirical assessment of that choice. The explicit sampling assumption and confidence-interval descriptions also help readers assess the evidence. These gains are tempered by conflicting statistical-reporting descriptions and the erroneous three-way characterization of AG-NEWS.
